(This evening through Tuesday)...
Issued at 258 PM EST Tue Nov 10 2026

A subtle surface trough is progressing through Indiana this 
afternoon and a wind shift has occurred around 1pm. Winds were light 
out of the southwest and are now out of the north-northwest from 
Indianapolis northward. This weak boundary is expected to stall 
across central Indiana this evening.

Winds should become light and variable overnight as the boundary 
layer stabilizes. With clear skies in place we are expecting 
excellent radiational cooling potential overnight. We have therefore 
went a bit below guidance for low temperatures with weight towards 
MOS and high-res short term guidance. This leads to forecast low 
temperatures in the upper 30s over rural areas and low 40s in 
urbanized locations.

With subtle moisture convergence in place along the weak boundary, 
patchy fog is possible overnight given the ideal radiative cooling 
potnetial. Fog may be locally dense along the axis of the boundary 
once it stalls. Areas from Terre Haute to Indianapolis eastward have 
the best chance of locally dense fog. Elsewhere, fog is possible but 
to a lesser degree.

Wednesday...

Satellite shows a potent vort max over the Dakotas as of this 
writing (1pm Tuesday). This system is diving southeastward embedded 
within broad west-northwesterly flow aloft. Ensemble guidance shows 
the vort max amplifying with time as it moves towards Indiana. This 
amplification will help induce surface cyclogenesis tonight. By 
Wednesday morning, all guidance shows a closed surface low over 
northern Illinois roughly around 1007mb. Surface winds around the 
developing low increase throughout the day Wednesday, with a cold 
front taking shape by mid day.

A narrow band of higher moisture is modeled to lift northward along 
and ahead of the cold front. With cooling temperatures aloft, lapse 
rates are expected to increase allowing for modest MLCAPE around 500 
J/Kg. Shear may be quite robust, between 35-45kt effective, 
especially across southern Indiana. Shear vectors are easterly and 
perpendicular to the cold front. As such, cellular/discrete 
convection is anticipated with eventual upscale growth.

As for potential hazards, it appears the isolated strong/damaging 
wind gust are the most probable. With steep lapse rates it wouldn't 
take much to mix some momentum aloft to the surface. However, the 
low-level jet appears quite weak so the threat will be limited. 
There is enough low-level shear and turning with height to allow for 
a very isolated tornado threat. This is dependent on how much 
moisture lifts northward and how strong the low-level jet gets. 
Right now, this threat appears to be a very low chance...but worth 
mentioning. Some small hail is possible but potential updraft 
strength does not appear enough for severe hail.

Wednesday Night into Friday...

Strong northerly flow behind Wednesday's departing system will lead 
to wind gusts in the 30-40 mph range. Cold air advection should 
limit temperature recovery during the day Thursday. Lows in the 
lower 40s may only rebound into the upper 40s despite some sunshine 
peeking through. Additionally, precipitation is likely to develop by 
mid day Thursday as the core of the upper-level vort max arrives. 
Steeping lapse rates and fetch off of Lake Michigan should lead to 
showery/convective precipitation. Temperatures aloft may be cold 
enough for graupel or snow to mix in at times late Thursday into 
Thursday night. Precipitation diminishes for most of the region by 
sunset with only a narrow band lingering immediately downwind of 
Lake Michigan. Lows Thursday night into Friday morning look to be in 
the low to mid 30s. Highs friday top out in the high 40s mostly 
cloudy skies. Clouds should begin clearing during the afternoon but 
may persist longer downwind of the lake.

Saturday through Early Next Week...

The upper low will shift east into the Canadian Maritimes by Sunday 
with an overall transition to broad ridging aloft that will persist 
well into next week. Widespread near to below freezing temperatures 
are expected on Saturday and Sunday mornings under clear skies and 
light winds. Other than the potential for lingering scattered 
diurnal cu on Saturday as the upper low moves away... expect a 
return to mainly clear skies that will likely extend into the middle 
of next week as strong high pressure settles over the region. The 
onset of warm advection will usher in a slow warming trend with 
highs rising from the mid and upper 40s on Saturday back into the 
mid and upper 50s by next Tuesday and Wednesday.
